description: Update an existing sequence: both its settings and its steps. Sequence-level settings live directly on this tool - name, description, labels, trigger (with its trigger-specific field), enrollmentMode plus enrollmentFieldPath, enrollmentPaused, userCancellable, activeSubscribersOnly, stopCondition, sendingWindow, frequencyCapEnabled, bccEmails, and the sender/reply identity. This is the only way to change enrollmentMode after create_sequence, so use it to move a tag- or event-triggered sequence off the default 'unlimited' re-entry to 'one_time' or 'matching_field'. To target a specific existing step, use IDs returned by get_sequence. The emails/steps arrays edit email steps, smsSteps edits SMS steps, and subscriberUpdateSteps replaces the config of action_update_attributes steps. The emails/steps arrays reach action_email steps only: an action_ab_test step keeps its copy on the A/B test variants, so read variant blocks from get_sequence.sequence.emails[].abTest.variants and change each variant with update_ab_test_variant. If update_ab_test_variant is not in the tool list, enable it on the Sequenzy connector rather than writing through update_template. To insert new linear steps, use insertSteps with an afterNodeId from get_sequence; omit afterNodeId only to append to an unambiguous linear tail. Deleting a step immediately moves parked recipients to its unique surviving successor, or completes them when no successor remains; inspect migratedRecipientCount and completedRecipientCount in the returned sequence. For active sequences, structural changes such as insertSteps or branch require confirmStructuralChange:true after the user confirms the live-flow impact.

activeSubscribersOnly.description: Only enroll contacts whose status is active. Defaults to false, where unsubscribed and bounced contacts still enter on tag, event, list or contact triggers so non-marketing steps (tags, webhooks, transactional emails) run for them, and their marketing emails are skipped at send time. Set true to keep them out entirely. Pending double opt-in contacts still wait for confirmation.

audienceAutoEnroll.description: Manual countdowns only: keep enrolling people who join the audience later (new list members, new segment matches) until the last key date passes, landing them on the current step. { audience, enabled? } where audience has the enroll_sequence_audience shape; enabled defaults to true. Switching on enrolls the current audience right away and re-checks every few minutes. It ends itself after the last key date.

audience.description: Who to enroll. { type: 'all' } for every active contact with an email, { type: 'lists', listIds: [...] }, { type: 'segment', segmentId: '...' }, { type: 'filtered', filters: [...] } with subscriber filters, or { type: 'rules', include: [...], exclude: [...] } combining several. For hand-picked contacts beyond the 500 cap of enroll_subscribers_in_sequence, use { type: 'rules', include: [], includedSubscriberIds: [...] }. Same shape as campaign targetLists.

excludedCampaignOpenerIds.description: Exclude contacts who opened any of these campaigns.

excludedSubscriberIds.description: Contacts removed from the include rules. Does not remove includedSubscriberIds.

includedSubscriberIds.description: Specific contacts to enroll in addition to the include rules. Unsubscribed, bounced and email-less contacts are skipped.

startsAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time before which no sync runs, e.g. the scheduledFor of the initial enrollment, so late joiners are not enrolled ahead of everyone else.

bccEmails.description: Email addresses that receive a blind copy of every email this sequence sends, such as a customer support inbox (max 10). Omit to leave unchanged. Use clearBccEmails to remove them.

branch.description: Insert an if/else branch into an existing sequence. Use get_sequence first to choose afterNodeId and existing target nodes. Each conditional path can provide new steps, targetNodeId, or both; the else path uses elseSteps and/or elseTargetNodeId. A target may be the completion node. Empty paths require allowEmptyPaths:true. Conditions support tag presence/absence, lists, saved segments, events, clicked links, and field comparisons. Use activityScope for event_received and link_clicked checks.

afterNodeId.description: Existing node ID to insert the branch after. Use a nodeId from get_sequence.sequence.nodes or get_sequence.sequence.emails.

allowEmptyPaths.description: Set true only when intentionally creating UI placeholders. A path with targetNodeId is already explicit and does not need this flag.

branches.description: Branch paths. On the default condition split they are evaluated in order and an else fallback is created automatically. On a random split (splitMode 'random') each entry is a weighted variant, conditionType and condition-specific fields are omitted, and there is no else path. Each path can create steps, route directly to an existing targetNodeId, or do both.

activityScope.description: Scope for event_received and link_clicked. Use this_sequence to restrict activity to the current enrollment.

conditionType.description: Condition for this path. has_phone, sms_subscribed and has_push_device need no resource fields. has_push_device passes when the contact has an active push device on a platform the workspace has push credentials for, unless its app reports notifications denied or not yet asked. Required unless the branch sets splitMode 'random', where paths are chosen by percentage and this field must be omitted.

eventName.description: Event name for event_received, for example email.replied.

fieldName.description: Subscriber attribute name/path for field conditions.

id.description: Optional stable path ID. Defaults to branch-0, branch-1, and so on. The value 'else' is reserved.

label.description: Display label, for example 'Replied in this sequence'.

linkUrl.description: Optional URL substring for link_clicked. Omit to match any tracked click.

steps.description: Optional new steps for this path. When targetNodeId is also set, the last new step connects to that existing node.

items.description: A typed step to create inside a sequence path, including email, SMS, delay, discount, subscriber actions, conditions, waits, webhooks, and AI steps.

attachments.description: Email only: URL-backed file attachments (max 10, 15MB total per email). path may be a public HTTPS URL or an {{event.*}} URL template resolved from the enrollment event at send time.

bccEmails.description: Email only: addresses BCC'd on this step in addition to sequence BCC.

blocks.description:
Sequenzy email blocks. Provide blocks or html for email steps. For migrated provider HTML, prefer `html`; Sequenzy stores it as one raw HTML block and does not recreate it as native blocks. Use `styles` for per-block background, background opacity, text color, padding, border radius, border width, and border color. Recolor body copy with `styles.textColor` (or the top-level `textColor` alias), not with an inline `style` on `

` or ``. Top-level style aliases such as `backgroundColor`, `backgroundOpacity`, `textColor`, `textAlign`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, and `borderRadius` are also accepted and saved under `styles`. Blocks can include repeat blocks over array variables such as items. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes. Any block accepts a `conditions` array so it only renders for matching recipients; conditions must all match unless the block sets `conditionsMatch: "any"`, and a numeric path segment reads one list item (`goals.0:bias`). To branch on a value passed in transactional `variables` or an automation `event` payload, use { "id": "c1", "field": "variable", "operator": "is", "value": "plan:pro" }; "attribute" uses the same "name:value" form, while "email"/"firstName"/"lastName" use a plain comparison value. Live subscriber fields are "status", "tag", "list", "segment", "event", "emailProvider", "phone", "phoneCountry", "smsStatus", "added", "stripeProduct", "stripeCurrentProduct", "stripeTrialProduct", "commerceProduct", "commerceCollection", "emailSent", "emailDelivered", "emailOpened", "emailClicked", "emailBounced", and "emailComplained". They use the same field-specific values and operators as segment filters, for example { "id": "c2", "field": "segment", "operator": "is", "value": "seg_123" }, { "id": "c3", "field": "tag", "operator": "contains", "value": "vip" }, or { "id": "c4", "field": "event", "operator": "at_least", "value": "purchase:3:30d" }. Supported operators across fields are is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, not_starts_with, gt, gte, lt, lte, less_than, more_than, at_least, less_than_count, is_empty, is_not_empty, is_temporary_bounce, and is_permanent_bounce; each field accepts only its segment-filter operators. Recipients without a stored subscriber match use the OTHERWISE branch or hide a conditionally displayed block. For if/else, use a { type: "conditional-group", conditions: [...], ifBranch: { children: [...] }, elseBranch: { children: [...] } } block. `styles` applies to the block's own container, not to an inner rendered element. On a button block, `styles.backgroundColor` colors the band behind the button and `styles.textColor` does not reach the label - set the top-level `buttonColor` and `buttonTextColor` fields instead, or leave them unset to inherit the email theme's primary color. Unsupported fields are discarded and reported in the response `warnings` array rather than rejected. Polls and NPS surveys use a native poll block. For answer buttons use { "type": "poll", "variant": "options", "question": "What did you think?", "options": [{ "label": "Loved it", "value": "loved" }, { "label": "Not for me", "value": "not_for_me" }], "attributeKey": "email_feedback" }. For NPS use { "type": "poll", "variant": "nps", "question": "How likely are you to recommend us?", "options": [], "attributeKey": "nps_score", "npsLowLabel": "Not likely", "npsHighLabel": "Very likely" }. `attributeKey` stores the latest response for segmentation. Set `allowMultiple: true` on a text-only options poll to let recipients pick several answers: answer links then open a hosted selection page where the recipient checks any number of options and saves them in one submit, and `attributeKey` stores the list of selected values (filter with attribute `contains`). Multi-select polls cannot use option images or configurations whose encoded signed links exceed the delivery-safe size limit. Optional `appearance` picks the answer style: "soft" (default), "pill", "outline", "filled", "pop" (hard-shadow boxes), "brutal" (square uppercase slabs), "quiz" (A/B/C letter badges), or "minimal" (bare ruled rows). `accentColor` recolors every appearance, including "brutal". `optionRadius` sets answer-button corners in px (0 is square) independently of `styles.borderRadius`, while `questionColor` recolors only the question. `fontFamily` applies to the poll; `optionFontSize`, `optionFontWeight`, `optionLetterSpacing`, and `optionTextTransform` style answers, and the matching `questionFontSize`, `questionFontWeight`, `questionLetterSpacing`, and `questionTextTransform` fields style the question. Sizes and spacing are px, weights are 100-900, and transforms are "none" or "uppercase". Optional `confirmationMessage` customizes the hosted thank-you page; set `redirectUrl` only when respondents should land on another page. For a new image, call `upload_image_asset` first and insert its returned `imageBlock`. A responsive fixed-height screenshot crop uses { "type": "image", "src": "https://...", "alt": "Product dashboard", "width": 100, "widthType": "percent", "height": 320, "objectFit": "cover", "align": "center" }. A YouTube video block can override its still with { "type": "video", "videoUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...", "thumbnailUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/cover.jpg", "alt": "Watch the product tour" }. Replacing the blocks array without `thumbnailUrl` restores YouTube's own thumbnail; the video destination remains `videoUrl`. Minimal valid core examples: {"type":"heading","content":"Title","level":1}; {"type":"text","content":"

Paragraph with bold

","variant":"paragraph"}; {"type":"list","variant":"bullet","items":[{"content":"First point"},{"content":"Second point"}]}; {"type":"steps","variant":"timeline","items":[{"title":"Connect","description":"Link your account."},{"title":"Launch","description":"Send your first campaign."}]}; {"type":"button","text":"Click Me","url":"https://example.com","variant":"primary"}; {"type":"image","src":"https://...","alt":"Description","width":100,"widthType":"percent","height":240,"objectFit":"cover","href":"https://example.com","align":"center"}. Heading and text use `content`; button uses `text` but also accepts `content` as an alias and defaults `variant` to `primary`. Image `widthType` accepts `percent` or `px`. Lists are their own block type, never a text variant: `text` accepts only variant paragraph, lead, or html and never accepts `items`, so a numbered list is {"type":"list","variant":"numbered","items":[{"content":"First"}]} and a visual numbered walkthrough is {"type":"steps","variant":"numbered","items":[{"title":"Step one","description":"What happens"},{"title":"Step two","description":"What happens next"}]}. List items carry `content`; steps items carry `title` plus an optional `description`. A list item nests under the item above it with `indent` 1 or 2. Call `get_email_block_schema` for the required and optional fields of any other block type. If that tool is not in the MCP tool list, enable it on the Sequenzy connector rather than inferring fields from live HTML; the same reference is also at `sequenzy://email-blocks` (MCP resource), `GET /api/v1/email-blocks` (API), and `sequenzy blocks ` (CLI).

buttons.description: In-app: up to 2 {label, action: open_url|dismiss|request_push_permission, url} buttons; request_push_permission asks for notification permission.

ccEmails.description: Email only: addresses CC'd on this step.

config.description: Config for advanced nodeType steps. Required fields depend on nodeType: action_add_tag and action_remove_tag need tagId or tagName; action_add_to_list and action_remove_from_list need listId; action_update_attributes uses the Update Subscriber fields (firstName, lastName, status, customAttributeUpdates) and may use trigger-event merge tags; logic_wait_for_event needs eventName plus optional timeoutDays and timeoutAction; logic_condition needs conditionType plus that condition's resource field; action_webhook needs an HTTPS url plus optional method, headers, body, resultKey, and onError; action_ai generates short per-contact fragments (a sentence or two each) that later email steps insert with {{ai.KEY.field}} merge tags, not whole emails, and needs prompt, resultKey, and outputFields plus optional includeTags, includeEventProperties, includeRecentEvents, recentEventLimit, includeAttributes, and onError; logic_delay uses delayDays/delayHours/delayMinutes. Fields that do not apply to the node type are dropped.

activityScope.description: logic_condition: scope for event_received and link_clicked. Use this_sequence to restrict activity to the current enrollment.

body.description: action_webhook: optional JSON body template for POST/PUT/PATCH. Must be valid JSON as written, with merge tags inside quoted string values ({"email": "{{email}}"}); a tag in a bare value position is rejected. Tags are resolved at execution time; when omitted, the default payload with subscriber and sequence context is sent.

conditionType.description: logic_condition: condition evaluated before continuing. has_phone, sms_subscribed and has_push_device need no resource fields. has_push_device passes when the contact has an active push device on a platform the workspace has push credentials for, unless its app reports notifications denied or not yet asked.

value.description: Literal scalar, null to delete, or a standalone merge tag such as {{event.plan}}, {{event.amount}}, or {{event.active}}.

eventName.description: logic_wait_for_event and event_received conditions: event to wait for or check, for example email.replied.

fieldName.description: logic_condition: subscriber attribute name/path for field comparisons.

fieldValue.description: logic_condition: comparison value for field comparisons.

firstName.description: First name literal or merge tag; null clears the field.

headers.description: action_webhook: optional string-valued request headers. Values support merge tags. Secret values are redacted on sequence reads.

includeAttributes.description: action_ai: custom attribute keys to include in the prompt context (max 30). Only the listed keys are sent.

includeEventProperties.description: action_ai: include the enrollment's trigger event name and properties in the prompt context.

includeRecentEvents.description: action_ai: include the contact's most recent custom events (newest first) in the prompt context.

includeTags.description: action_ai: include the contact's tags in the prompt context.

lastName.description: Last name literal or merge tag; null clears the field.

linkUrl.description: logic_condition: optional URL substring for link_clicked. Omit to match any tracked click.

listId.description: action_add_to_list / action_remove_from_list / in_list: list ID. It must match an existing list in this company; listName is filled in for you.

listName.description: Optional cached list display name for list actions.

method.description: action_webhook: HTTP method. Defaults to POST.

onError.description: action_webhook / action_ai: behavior when the step fails. continue proceeds to the next step, exit ends the sequence for the subscriber, fail marks the enrollment failed. Defaults to fail for webhooks and continue for AI steps (fallbacks fill the output fields).

outputFields.description: action_ai: named values the model must return (1-10). Each key becomes a {{ai.KEY.<key>}} merge tag for later steps. fallback is used when generation fails, so emails still send with sensible copy. Combined field maxLength values must fit the step's conservative 2000-token multilingual response budget plus JSON overhead.

description.description: What the model should produce for this field, e.g. 'A subject line under 50 characters'. Max 300 chars.

fallback.description: Text used verbatim when generation fails or the model omits the field.

key.description: Field key, e.g. subject_line. Must start with a letter; letters, numbers, underscores; max 64 chars; unique within the step.

maxLength.description: Hard cap on stored characters (1-4000). Defaults to 500. Output beyond it is cut.

prompt.description: action_ai: prompt template sent to the model, resolved per contact at execution time. Supports merge tags like {{first_name}}, {{event.plan}}, and {{webhooks.KEY.data.field}}. Max 8000 chars.

recentEventLimit.description: action_ai: how many recent events to include when includeRecentEvents is true (1-50, default 10).

resultKey.description: action_webhook / action_ai: where the result is saved. Later steps reference it via {{webhooks.KEY.data.field}} (webhook) or {{ai.KEY.field}} (AI) merge tags. Required for action_ai. Must start with a letter; letters, numbers, underscores; max 64 chars.

tagId.description: action_add_tag / action_remove_tag: tag ID. Pass a name in tagName instead, because tag actions resolve tagId by ID only. has_tag / does_not_have_tag also accept a tag name here. Missing tag definitions are created automatically.

tagName.description: action_add_tag / action_remove_tag / has_tag / does_not_have_tag: tag name. Use instead of tagId when you only know the name.

timeoutAction.description: logic_wait_for_event: continue to the next node or exit the sequence when the timeout is reached. Defaults to continue.

timeoutDays.description: logic_wait_for_event: maximum wait in whole days from 1 to 365. Defaults to 7.

url.description: action_webhook: destination HTTPS URL called when a subscriber reaches this step. Supports merge tags like {{email}} and {{event.order_id}} resolved at execution time.

data.description: In-app: string key/values passed to the app.

delay.description: Fixed delay before this step. For a dynamic wait-until-date delay, either set mode:'until_date' plus untilDateField here, or use waitUntil. For a wait-until-weekday-window delay, either set mode:'until_weekday' plus untilDays/untilStartTime/untilTimezone here, or use waitUntilWeekday (use waitUntilWeekday.minimumWait to wait a few days first; days/hours/minutes here are ignored in that mode).

mode.description: Use duration for a fixed wait, until_date to resolve a date from the trigger event or a contact attribute, until_weekday to wait for the next weekday/time window, or until_key_date to wait relative to a sequence key date (prefer waitUntilKeyDate).

untilDateField.description: For mode:'until_date', dot-path into the trigger event properties or, with untilDateSource attribute, the contact's custom attributes.

untilDateSource.description: For mode:'until_date', read untilDateField from the trigger event (event, default) or the contact's custom attributes (attribute).

untilDays.description: For mode:'until_weekday', weekday names the wait may release on.

untilEndTime.description: For mode:'until_weekday', window end in 24-hour HH:mm local time. Defaults to the end-of-day boundary 24:00.

untilKeyDate.description: For mode:'until_key_date', the key of a sequence key date.

untilMissingAction.description: For mode:'until_date', what to do when the field is missing or invalid. Defaults to continue.

untilOffsetDirection.description: For mode:'until_date', whether days/hours/minutes are before or after the resolved date. Defaults to after.

untilPastAction.description: For mode:'until_key_date' or 'until_date', what late enrollees do when the moment already passed. Defaults to skip for until_key_date and continue for until_date.

untilStartTime.description: For mode:'until_weekday', window start in 24-hour HH:mm local time.

untilTimezone.description: For mode:'until_weekday', IANA timezone the window is evaluated in (fallback for untilTimezoneSource subscriber).

untilTimezoneSource.description: For mode:'until_weekday': fixed (default) or subscriber (each contact's timezone, else untilTimezone).

delayMs.description: Delay in milliseconds. Useful for standalone type:'delay' steps.

discount.description: Discount configuration for create_discount steps. Same shape as create_sequence steps. The code is minted per subscriber at run time and reaches every later email in the same sequence as {{discount.code}}. Also available: {{discount.value}} (pre-formatted, e.g. "20% off" or "$10 off"), {{discount.percentOff}}, {{discount.amountOff}}, {{discount.currency}}, and {{date.discount.expiresAt}} (locale-formatted expiry). Present the code with a { "type": "discount-code", "code": "{{discount.code}}", "label": "Your discount code" } block, or inline {{discount.code}} in any text block. These tags resolve only in emails downstream of the discount step; render_email substitutes a clearly fake sample code so the email can be previewed before anyone is enrolled, and lists anything it could not resolve under unresolvedMergeTags.

expiresAfterDays.description: In-app: days in the feed (messages default 30).

eyebrow.description: In-app: short line above the title, e.g. '3 days left'. Merge tags work.

format.description: In-app message format (default modal). html: custom HTML in `html`; title becomes its accessible name.

fromEmail.description: From address for this email step. Its domain must be verified. Mutually exclusive with senderProfileId.

fromName.description: Display name override for this email step. With fromEmail, also names a newly created sender profile.

html.description: HTML content for email steps. Stored as one raw HTML block. Use this for imported provider HTML. In-app format html: the message document (100 KB max; see validate_in_app_html).

iconUrl.description: Push only: optional https web push icon.

imagePlacement.description: In-app modals and full screens with an image: top (default, image above the text) or background (image fills the message, text on a dark scrim).

imageUrl.description: Push and in-app: optional https image.

imageUrls.description: SMS only: up to two public MMS image URLs.

ineligibleAction.description: SMS and push: behavior when the contact cannot receive the message.

isTransactional.description: Email only: omit the marketing unsubscribe footer.

kind.description: In-app: message (default, shown once), card, or placement (shown inline in a placement slot; needs `placement`).

label.description: Node label for discount or advanced node steps.

layout.description: In-app kind placement: card (default; image over the text, link buttons), banner (compact row with an image thumbnail and a filled button) or hero (text over the image, filled button).

name.description: Email template name for email steps.

nodeType.description: Advanced sequence path node type. Prefer type unless creating a non-email action. Tag, list, subscriber-update, wait, condition, webhook, and AI node types carry their fields in config, for example nodeType:'action_add_tag' with config:{ tagName:'newsletter-confirmed' }. SMS steps still use the step-level text/imageUrls/ineligibleAction, discount steps the step-level discount fields, and delays the step-level delay/delayMs/waitUntil.

placement.description: In-app kind placement: key of the workspace placement to fill (list_in_app_placements).

platforms.description: Push only: limit delivery to these platforms.

position.description: In-app position. Banners: top or bottom (default). Modals: bottom (a sheet, default) or center.

priority.description: In-app kind placement: high, medium (default) or low. The highest-priority open item for a placement shows; ties go to the newest.

provider.description: Discount provider. Use stripe to dynamically create a Stripe coupon plus promotion code, or shopify to dynamically create a Shopify Admin discount code.

replyProfileId.description: Reply profile for this email step. Omit to inherit the effective Reply-To of the nearest sequence email. After a branch merge, only fields shared by every incoming path are inherited; conflicting fields use sequence or company defaults.

replyTo.description: Reply-To address for this email step. Mutually exclusive with replyProfileId.

replyToName.description: Reply-To display name override for this email step. Requires replyTo; omit it when using replyProfileId, which already carries its own display name.

senderProfileId.description: Sender profile for this email step. Omit to inherit the effective identity of the nearest sequence email. After a branch merge, only fields shared by every incoming path are inherited; conflicting fields use sequence or company defaults.

showCloseButton.description: In-app format html: native close button (default true); off when the HTML closes itself.

style.description: In-app look: {preset: brand|soft|bold|dark, backgroundColor, textColor, buttonColor, buttonTextColor (#rrggbb), cornerRadius 0-32, buttonRadius 0-40}. Colors default to the brand; updates merge, null resets.

subject.description: Email subject. Required for email steps.

type.description: Sequence path step type. Omit for email steps; use delay for fixed/date waits or update_subscriber for action_update_attributes. For an event gate, use nodeType:'logic_wait_for_event' with an explicit config object. A path is one linear chain, so it cannot contain a nested 'logic_branch' step: end the path with the step the nested branch should follow, then insert that branch with its own insert_sequence_step call using an afterNodeId from addedBranchPathNodeIds.

url.description: Push only: https link or app deep link opened on tap.

waitUntil.description: Wait until a date from the trigger event or a contact attribute before this step. Use this for renewal reminders, appointment follow-ups, trial-expiry nudges, due-date or anniversary timelines, and other subscriber-specific dates. The field value must be an ISO date string or Unix timestamp. For a per-contact timeline that contacts can join late (e.g. emails at 20, 12 and 4 weeks before a dueDate attribute), use source attribute with pastAction skip on every wait so late joiners only get the steps still ahead, and pastAction continue on a final wait that everyone should reach.

days.description: Offset days shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

direction.description: Whether the offset applies before or after the resolved date. Defaults to after.

field.description: Dot-path into the trigger event properties (source event) or the contact's custom attributes (source attribute), e.g. renews_at, booking.startsAt or dueDate.

hours.description: Offset hours shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

minutes.description: Offset minutes shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

missingAction.description: What to do if the date field is missing or invalid. Defaults to continue.

offset.description: Offset relative to a wait-until date.

pastAction.description: What to do when the date (after the offset) already passed when the contact reaches this wait. continue (default) moves on immediately, skip skips the following email and action steps until the next wait, condition or branch, exit ends the enrollment. Omitted waitUntil fields reset to their defaults when updating a step, so resend source and pastAction.

source.description: Where field is read from. event (default) reads the trigger event properties and needs an event trigger. attribute reads the contact's custom attributes when the step is reached, so it works with any trigger. If the date moves later while a contact is waiting, the contact waits for the new date; moving it earlier does not release them sooner, and a date removed while waiting follows missingAction.

waitUntilKeyDate.description: Wait relative to one of the sequence's key dates before this step, e.g. { key: 'black_friday_starts', days: 7, direction: 'before' } or { key: 'black_friday_ends', hours: 1 }. The key must exist in the sequence's keyDates. pastAction decides what a late enrollee does when the moment already passed: skip (default) skips the following steps until the next wait, continue sends immediately, exit ends the enrollment. Use with a manual trigger for one-time countdown campaigns.

days.description: Offset days shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

direction.description: Whether the offset applies before or after the key date. Defaults to before.

hours.description: Offset hours shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

minutes.description: Offset minutes shorthand. Ignored when offset is provided.

missingAction.description: What to do if the key date no longer exists. Defaults to exit.

offset.description: Offset relative to a wait-until date.

pastAction.description: What late enrollees do when the moment already passed. Defaults to skip.

waitUntilWeekday.description: Wait until the next occurrence of a weekday inside a local-time window before this step, e.g. { day: 'sunday', startTime: '09:00', endTime: '12:00', timezone: 'America/Los_Angeles' }. timezoneSource: 'subscriber' uses each contact's own timezone. Continues immediately when the step is reached inside the window, so a Sunday-morning enrollment is not pushed a full week. Add minimumWait: { days: 6 } to wait at least that long first and then release at the next window: one step instead of a fixed delay followed by a separate weekday wait. Place it immediately before the email when the send day matters - it controls when the flow resumes, so any step between it and the email shifts the send off the window (a sequence-level sendingWindow only holds emails at send time; it does not reschedule the graph).

day.description: Single weekday convenience alias for days, e.g. sunday or sun.

days.description: Weekdays the wait may release on. Full or short names such as sunday, sun. The nearest upcoming day wins.

endTime.description: Window end in 24-hour HH:mm local time. Defaults to the end-of-day boundary 24:00. If the wake-up is missed past endTime (rare operational failure), the wait rolls to the next configured day instead of releasing late.

minimumWait.description: Wait at least this long before looking for the window, e.g. { days: 6 }. Once it ends, the contact continues at that moment if it falls inside the window, otherwise at the next window opening. Omit for no minimum.

startTime.description: Window start in 24-hour HH:mm local time, e.g. 09:00. Required.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the window is evaluated in, e.g. America/Los_Angeles. Required; the fallback for timezoneSource 'subscriber'.

timezoneSource.description: fixed (default): timezone for everyone. subscriber: each contact's timezone, else timezone; re-read on resume.

tagId.description: Tag ID or tag name for has_tag and does_not_have_tag.

tagName.description: Tag name for has_tag and does_not_have_tag. This can be used instead of tagId.

targetNodeId.description: Optional existing node to route this branch path to. Use a node ID from get_sequence, including the sequence completion node when this path should stop. If steps are also provided, they run before this target.

elseSteps.description: Optional new steps inside the else fallback path. Not valid on a random split. Same schema as `branch.branches[].steps` in this tool.

elseTargetNodeId.description: Optional existing node to route the else path to. Use a node ID from get_sequence, including the completion node. If elseSteps are also provided, they run before this target.

randomPercentages.description: Required when splitMode is 'random': one non-negative percentage per entry in branches, in the same order, summing to 100. For an even two-way test use [50, 50].

splitMode.description: How subscribers are routed. 'condition' (default) evaluates each branch's conditionType in order. 'random' assigns each subscriber a path by percentage when they reach the node, which is how you build a concurrent A/B split inside a sequence - for example testing two abandoned-cart offers against each other at the same time instead of running them one after another. Random splits require randomPercentages, omit conditionType and condition-specific fields on every branch, and must not define an else path. To A/B test the content of a single existing email step instead of branching the flow, use create_ab_test with automationNodeId, which tracks variants and picks a winner for you.

clearAudienceAutoEnroll.description: Set true to stop auto-enrolling later joiners. Do not provide this together with audienceAutoEnroll.

clearBccEmails.description: Set true to remove the sequence BCC addresses. Do not provide this together with bccEmails.

clearEnrollmentFieldPath.description: Set true to clear enrollmentFieldPath without sending a nullable schema value.

clearKeyDates.description: Set true to remove every key date. Rejected while a delay step still waits for one of them. Do not provide this together with keyDates.

clearSendingWindow.description: Set true to remove the sequence sending window. Do not provide this together with sendingWindow.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

confirmLiveChange.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirms replacing the trigger of an active sequence. Required with trigger when the sequence is active.

confirmStructuralChange.description: Set true only after the user explicitly confirms a structural edit to an active sequence. Required for insertSteps or branch when the sequence is active; not needed for content-only email edits.

customIntegration.description: Typed custom inbound webhook descriptor used instead of a catalog integration.

description.description: Sequence description shown in the dashboard.

emails.description: Updated existing sequence emails. If you omit emailId/nodeId, items are matched by existing step order. This field does not create new steps; use insertSteps for insertion and include delay on inserted email steps when a timer is needed.

attachments.description: URL-backed file attachments for this email step (max 10, 15MB total per email). path may be a public HTTPS URL or an {{event.*}} URL template resolved from the enrollment event at send time. Pass [] to remove all attachments.

blocks.description:
Replacement Sequenzy email blocks. Use `styles` for per-block background, background opacity, text color, padding, border radius, border width, and border color. Recolor body copy with `styles.textColor` (or the top-level `textColor` alias), not with an inline `style` on `

` or ``. Top-level style aliases such as `backgroundColor`, `backgroundOpacity`, `textColor`, `textAlign`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, and `borderRadius` are also accepted and saved under `styles`. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes. Any block accepts a `conditions` array so it only renders for matching recipients; conditions must all match unless the block sets `conditionsMatch: "any"`, and a numeric path segment reads one list item (`goals.0:bias`). To branch on a value passed in transactional `variables` or an automation `event` payload, use { "id": "c1", "field": "variable", "operator": "is", "value": "plan:pro" }; "attribute" uses the same "name:value" form, while "email"/"firstName"/"lastName" use a plain comparison value. Live subscriber fields are "status", "tag", "list", "segment", "event", "emailProvider", "phone", "phoneCountry", "smsStatus", "added", "stripeProduct", "stripeCurrentProduct", "stripeTrialProduct", "commerceProduct", "commerceCollection", "emailSent", "emailDelivered", "emailOpened", "emailClicked", "emailBounced", and "emailComplained". They use the same field-specific values and operators as segment filters, for example { "id": "c2", "field": "segment", "operator": "is", "value": "seg_123" }, { "id": "c3", "field": "tag", "operator": "contains", "value": "vip" }, or { "id": "c4", "field": "event", "operator": "at_least", "value": "purchase:3:30d" }. Supported operators across fields are is, is_not, contains, not_contains, starts_with, not_starts_with, gt, gte, lt, lte, less_than, more_than, at_least, less_than_count, is_empty, is_not_empty, is_temporary_bounce, and is_permanent_bounce; each field accepts only its segment-filter operators. Recipients without a stored subscriber match use the OTHERWISE branch or hide a conditionally displayed block. For if/else, use a { type: "conditional-group", conditions: [...], ifBranch: { children: [...] }, elseBranch: { children: [...] } } block. `styles` applies to the block's own container, not to an inner rendered element. On a button block, `styles.backgroundColor` colors the band behind the button and `styles.textColor` does not reach the label - set the top-level `buttonColor` and `buttonTextColor` fields instead, or leave them unset to inherit the email theme's primary color. Unsupported fields are discarded and reported in the response `warnings` array rather than rejected. Polls and NPS surveys use a native poll block. For answer buttons use { "type": "poll", "variant": "options", "question": "What did you think?", "options": [{ "label": "Loved it", "value": "loved" }, { "label": "Not for me", "value": "not_for_me" }], "attributeKey": "email_feedback" }. For NPS use { "type": "poll", "variant": "nps", "question": "How likely are you to recommend us?", "options": [], "attributeKey": "nps_score", "npsLowLabel": "Not likely", "npsHighLabel": "Very likely" }. `attributeKey` stores the latest response for segmentation. Set `allowMultiple: true` on a text-only options poll to let recipients pick several answers: answer links then open a hosted selection page where the recipient checks any number of options and saves them in one submit, and `attributeKey` stores the list of selected values (filter with attribute `contains`). Multi-select polls cannot use option images or configurations whose encoded signed links exceed the delivery-safe size limit. Optional `appearance` picks the answer style: "soft" (default), "pill", "outline", "filled", "pop" (hard-shadow boxes), "brutal" (square uppercase slabs), "quiz" (A/B/C letter badges), or "minimal" (bare ruled rows). `accentColor` recolors every appearance, including "brutal". `optionRadius` sets answer-button corners in px (0 is square) independently of `styles.borderRadius`, while `questionColor` recolors only the question. `fontFamily` applies to the poll; `optionFontSize`, `optionFontWeight`, `optionLetterSpacing`, and `optionTextTransform` style answers, and the matching `questionFontSize`, `questionFontWeight`, `questionLetterSpacing`, and `questionTextTransform` fields style the question. Sizes and spacing are px, weights are 100-900, and transforms are "none" or "uppercase". Optional `confirmationMessage` customizes the hosted thank-you page; set `redirectUrl` only when respondents should land on another page. For a new image, call `upload_image_asset` first and insert its returned `imageBlock`. A responsive fixed-height screenshot crop uses { "type": "image", "src": "https://...", "alt": "Product dashboard", "width": 100, "widthType": "percent", "height": 320, "objectFit": "cover", "align": "center" }. A YouTube video block can override its still with { "type": "video", "videoUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=...", "thumbnailUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/cover.jpg", "alt": "Watch the product tour" }. Replacing the blocks array without `thumbnailUrl` restores YouTube's own thumbnail; the video destination remains `videoUrl`. Minimal valid core examples: {"type":"heading","content":"Title","level":1}; {"type":"text","content":"

","variant":"paragraph"}; {"type":"list","variant":"bullet","items":[{"content":"First point"},{"content":"Second point"}]}; {"type":"steps","variant":"timeline","items":[{"title":"Connect","description":"Link your account."},{"title":"Launch","description":"Send your first campaign."}]}; {"type":"button","text":"Click Me","url":"https://example.com","variant":"primary"}; {"type":"image","src":"https://...","alt":"Description","width":100,"widthType":"percent","height":240,"objectFit":"cover","href":"https://example.com","align":"center"}. Heading and text use `content`; button uses `text` but also accepts `content` as an alias and defaults `variant` to `primary`. Image `widthType` accepts `percent` or `px`. Lists are their own block type, never a text variant: `text` accepts only variant paragraph, lead, or html and never accepts `items`, so a numbered list is {"type":"list","variant":"numbered","items":[{"content":"First"}]} and a visual numbered walkthrough is {"type":"steps","variant":"numbered","items":[{"title":"Step one","description":"What happens"},{"title":"Step two","description":"What happens next"}]}. List items carry `content`; steps items carry `title` plus an optional `description`. A list item nests under the item above it with `indent` 1 or 2. Call `get_email_block_schema` for the required and optional fields of any other block type. If that tool is not in the MCP tool list, enable it on the Sequenzy connector rather than inferring fields from live HTML; the same reference is also at `sequenzy://email-blocks` (MCP resource), `GET /api/v1/email-blocks` (API), and `sequenzy blocks ` (CLI). Replacing a step's blocks keeps that step's existing Style > Format rather than the company default: a step that already had a logo or footer gets them back even if you omit them, and every block added that way is listed in the response `warnings`. Pass `emailPreset` to change the format. A step whose stored content is a single raw HTML block has no format, so replacing it with another single raw HTML block is stored exactly as sent; replacing it with native blocks converts the step and does add a footer.

emailId.description: Optional target linked email template ID for a step. Use the emailId returned in get_sequence.sequence.emails.

emailPreset.description: Per-email Style > Format for native Sequenzy blocks, including emails that contain supported custom HTML blocks. Minimal removes the company logo and uses the simple footer; branded restores the branded chrome. Does not change the company default. Not a lossless toggle: minimal deletes standalone logo blocks, so switching back to branded generates a new logo block with a new id and the company name as alt text - send the authored logo block in `blocks` alongside the branded update to keep it. Not supported when the entire email is standalone raw HTML and must not be combined with html/htmlContent.

emailTheme.description: Visual theme override for this step's linked email only; the company-wide default is left untouched, as is every other email. Partial update: the patch merges into this email's current theme, so `{ colors: { background: '#f3f4f6' } }` repaints the outer canvas and keeps its fonts, spacing, and other colors; use colors.content for the inner card and colors.surface for nested cards. A step with no override merges into the company theme rather than the platform preset. Pass null to drop the override so the step follows the company theme again. Numeric values are clamped to supported ranges. Use update_company to change the account-wide default instead.

buttonStyle.description: How primary buttons are filled: "solid" (default) or "outline" (transparent fill with a brand-color border).

buttonText.description: Label color for solid buttons. Omit to auto-derive a readable color from the button background.

content.description: Inner content card the blocks sit on. Omit to preserve its current value; when no content color is stored, the card follows background.

layout.description: Layout settings. Every field is a number except contentAlign.

contentAlign.description: Where the content column sits in a wide email client: "center" (default) or "left" (flush left, like a plain personal email; buttons, the logo and footers move left too unless set to right, or kept centered with block `styles.keepAlign: true`). Phones show the column full width either way.

presetId.description: Theme preset to base the theme on: default, soft, editorial, or bold.

typography.description: Type settings; numbers except the font-family stacks.

footerFontFamily.description: Footer font stack, also used by the auto-added footer. null removes it.

headingFontFamily.description: Font stack for headings when it differs from the email body font. Omit so headings inherit the email font.

headingFontWeight.description: Heading weight applied to all heading levels, 300-900. Omit for the per-level defaults.

headingLetterSpacing.description: Heading letter spacing in pixels (negative = tighter), clamped to -2..4. Omit for natural tracking.

fromEmail.description: From address for this step. Its domain must be configured and verified. Mutually exclusive with senderProfileId.

fromName.description: Display name override for this step. Alone it only changes the visible name; with fromEmail it also names a newly created sender profile.

html.description: Updated HTML content for imported provider markup. Raw HTML is stored as one opaque block. Sequenzy preserves that markup but does not add a company logo, branded native sections, or theme-driven block design. Use blocks for editor-native design, or a drafting prompt when you want Sequenzy to compose a new branded email. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes.

htmlContent.description: Alias for html for imported provider markup. Raw HTML is stored as one opaque block. Sequenzy preserves that markup but does not add a company logo, branded native sections, or theme-driven block design. Use blocks for editor-native design, or a drafting prompt when you want Sequenzy to compose a new branded email. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes.

nodeId.description: Optional target action_email node ID for a step. Use the nodeId returned in get_sequence.sequence.emails.

replyProfileId.description: Reply profile for this step's Reply-To. Mutually exclusive with replyTo.

replyTo.description: Reply-To address for this step. Mutually exclusive with replyProfileId.

replyToName.description: Reply-To display name override for this step. Requires replyTo; omit it when using replyProfileId, which already carries its own display name.

senderProfileId.description: Sender profile for this step's From identity. Mutually exclusive with fromEmail.

enrollmentFieldPath.description: Scalar dot-path event property used by enrollmentMode='matching_field', such as 'order.id' or 'product.providerVariantId'. Use 'organization.externalId' in a workspace with Organizations to run the sequence once per organization for organization events. Array traversal with [] is not supported; use propertyFilters for array matching. Omit to leave unchanged. Use clearEnrollmentFieldPath to clear it.

enrollmentMode.description: Updated sequence re-entry mode. Use this to move an existing sequence off the default 'unlimited', which re-enrolls a subscriber each time the trigger fires once their earlier run has ended (frequency triggers enroll each contact once). 'one_time' enters a subscriber once ever, even if that run ended early. 'matching_field' allows one run at a time per event field value and is only valid for event-based sequence triggers. Changes apply to future enrollments only.

enrollmentPaused.description: Set true to stop new enrollments for an active sequence while current recipients continue. Set false to resume new enrollments. The sequence must already be active.

eventName.description: Event name required for event_received, inbound_webhook, inactivity, and frequency trigger replacements.

frequencyCapEnabled.description: Whether this sequence respects the company frequency cap (see get_frequency_cap / set_frequency_cap). When true, an email step is skipped for a contact already at the cap and the contact continues to the next step; transactional steps are never skipped. Omit to leave unchanged.

fromEmail.description: Set the From address for all emails in this sequence. Its domain must be configured and verified.

fromName.description: Display name recipients see, e.g. 'Brennon at TradeTally'. Selects the sender identity of that name on fromEmail, creating it when the address has no identity by that name; the mailbox's other display names, and everything pinned to them, are untouched. Requires fromEmail; omit it when using senderProfileId, which already carries its own display name.

inactiveDays.description: Days without event activity required for an inactivity trigger.

inactivityBaseline.description: Baseline for subscribers who have never produced the inactivity event.

insertSteps.description: Insert one or more new linear steps into an existing sequence. Use get_sequence first, then pass afterNodeId to insert after a specific node. If afterNodeId is omitted, the steps are appended only when the sequence has exactly one linear tail. Inserted email steps require subject plus blocks or html.

afterNodeId.description: Existing node ID to insert after. Use a nodeId from get_sequence.sequence.nodes or get_sequence.sequence.emails. Omit only to append to an unambiguous linear tail.

steps.description: New steps to insert. Supports emails, delays, create_discount actions, webhooks, and other supported sequence path node types. Same schema as `branch.branches[].steps` in this tool.

integrationEventKey.description: Catalog integration event key for inbound_webhook.

keyDates.description: Named absolute moments the sequence counts down to, e.g. Black Friday. Delay steps use waitUntilKeyDate to wait relative to one of them, so the whole countdown is re-timed by editing these dates. Keys default to a slug of the label ("Black Friday starts" -> black_friday_starts). Changing a key date on a live sequence re-schedules contacts already waiting on it. Pass null (update_sequence: clearKeyDates) to remove all key dates.

at.description: ISO 8601 date-time with offset or Z, e.g. 2026-11-27T00:00:00-05:00.

key.description: Stable identifier used by waitUntilKeyDate.key (lowercase letters, digits, underscores). Defaults to a slug of the label.

label.description: Human label, e.g. Black Friday starts.

sendWindow.description: How sends timed from these moments are spread out so a whole audience is not emailed in the same second. Each contact gets their own stable send time within spreadOverHours: after the moment for steps at or after it, and in the hours leading up to the step's time for steps timed before it, so a deadline email always arrives before the deadline. Omit to keep the current spread (new sequences use 4 hours).

spreadOverHours.description: Spread each email over this many hours. 0 sends everyone at the exact time. Default 4.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the dates are shown and edited in, e.g. America/New_York.

labels.description: Replace dashboard labels by name. Missing labels are created; [] clears labels.

listId.description: List ID for a contact_added trigger replacement.

listIds.description: Several list IDs for a contact_added trigger replacement. Joining ANY of them enrolls the contact. Cannot be combined with listScope.

listScope.description: For a contact_added trigger replacement with no list. 'any_contact' (default) enrolls every contact added, even one that joins no list; 'any_list' waits for a list membership. Cannot be combined with listId or listIds.

minCount.description: Minimum event count for a frequency trigger.

propertyFilters.description: Optional event-property filters for event_received or inbound_webhook.

value.description: Scalar comparison value, or an array for one_of.

replyProfileId.description: Set an existing reply profile (see list_sender_profiles). It already supplies both the Reply-To address and display name, so send it on its own and omit replyTo and replyToName.

replyTo.description: Set the Reply-To address for all emails in this sequence.

replyToName.description: Display name for the Reply-To address. Requires replyTo; omit it when using replyProfileId, which already carries its own display name. An address carries one Reply-To name company-wide: if replyTo already has a saved profile under a different name, that saved name is kept and the response `warnings` array says so. Rename it with update_sender_profile (type 'reply') to change it everywhere.

segmentId.description: Saved segment ID required for a segment_entered or segment_exited trigger replacement.

senderProfileId.description: Set an existing sender profile (see list_sender_profiles). It already supplies both the From address and display name, so send it on its own and omit fromEmail and fromName. To keep this profile under a different display name, set fromName on the email steps instead, where it is a per-step override.

sendingWindow.description: Optional send window for every email step in the sequence. This is not Send Time Optimization: it is a shared allowed-hours gate, not per-subscriber predicted send times. STO is campaign-only (list_campaigns, get_campaign, update_campaign, schedule_campaign). When set, email actions that become due outside the window wait until the next allowed local time. Omit days to allow every day. Changing the window does not move contacts already waiting on a delay step - they keep their existing wait time, and narrowing the window can defer them to the next allowed day. Call realign_sequence_enrollments after the change to pull those waits back to the new opening.

days.description: Allowed local days. Use full names or short names such as monday, tuesday, mon, tue. Omit for every day.

enabled.description: Set false to disable the sending window when creating a sequence. For updates, prefer clearSendingWindow.

endTime.description: Latest local send cutoff in 24-hour HH:mm format, e.g. 20:00, or 24:00 for the end-of-day boundary. Must be later than startTime.

startTime.description: Earliest local send time in 24-hour HH:mm format, e.g. 08:00.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the window, e.g. Europe/Kiev or America/New_York.

smsSteps.description: Content updates for existing SMS steps, targeted by nodeId (an action_sms node from get_sequence.sequence.nodes). Content-only edits - use insertSteps to create new SMS steps.

blocks.description: Replacement SMS content blocks (text + image subset).

imageUrls.description: Up to 2 publicly reachable MMS image URLs. Only valid together with text.

ineligibleAction.description: Updated behavior when the contact can't receive SMS.

label.description: Updated display label for the step.

text.description: Replacement plain-text message body. Merge tags like {{FIRST_NAME}} work. Provide text or blocks, not both.

steps.description: Alias for emails. Supports the same fields and matching rules, and only edits existing email steps. Use insertSteps to create new steps.

attachments.description: URL-backed file attachments for this email step (max 10, 15MB total per email). path may be a public HTTPS URL or an {{event.*}} URL template resolved from the enrollment event at send time. Pass [] to remove all attachments.

","variant":"paragraph"}; {"type":"list","variant":"bullet","items":[{"content":"First point"},{"content":"Second point"}]}; {"type":"steps","variant":"timeline","items":[{"title":"Connect","description":"Link your account."},{"title":"Launch","description":"Send your first campaign."}]}; {"type":"button","text":"Click Me","url":"https://example.com","variant":"primary"}; {"type":"image","src":"https://...","alt":"Description","width":100,"widthType":"percent","height":240,"objectFit":"cover","href":"https://example.com","align":"center"}. Heading and text use `content`; button uses `text` but also accepts `content` as an alias and defaults `variant` to `primary`. Image `widthType` accepts `percent` or `px`. Lists are their own block type, never a text variant: `text` accepts only variant paragraph, lead, or html and never accepts `items`, so a numbered list is {"type":"list","variant":"numbered","items":[{"content":"First"}]} and a visual numbered walkthrough is {"type":"steps","variant":"numbered","items":[{"title":"Step one","description":"What happens"},{"title":"Step two","description":"What happens next"}]}. List items carry `content`; steps items carry `title` plus an optional `description`. A list item nests under the item above it with `indent` 1 or 2. Call `get_email_block_schema` for the required and optional fields of any other block type. If that tool is not in the MCP tool list, enable it on the Sequenzy connector rather than inferring fields from live HTML; the same reference is also at `sequenzy://email-blocks` (MCP resource), `GET /api/v1/email-blocks` (API), and `sequenzy blocks ` (CLI). Replacing a step's blocks keeps that step's existing Style > Format rather than the company default: a step that already had a logo or footer gets them back even if you omit them, and every block added that way is listed in the response `warnings`. Pass `emailPreset` to change the format. A step whose stored content is a single raw HTML block has no format, so replacing it with another single raw HTML block is stored exactly as sent; replacing it with native blocks converts the step and does add a footer.

emailId.description: Optional target linked email template ID for a step. Use the emailId returned in get_sequence.sequence.emails.

emailPreset.description: Per-email Style > Format for native Sequenzy blocks, including emails that contain supported custom HTML blocks. Minimal removes the company logo and uses the simple footer; branded restores the branded chrome. Does not change the company default. Not a lossless toggle: minimal deletes standalone logo blocks, so switching back to branded generates a new logo block with a new id and the company name as alt text - send the authored logo block in `blocks` alongside the branded update to keep it. Not supported when the entire email is standalone raw HTML and must not be combined with html/htmlContent.

emailTheme.description: Visual theme override for this step's linked email only; the company-wide default is left untouched, as is every other email. Partial update: the patch merges into this email's current theme, so `{ colors: { background: '#f3f4f6' } }` repaints the outer canvas and keeps its fonts, spacing, and other colors; use colors.content for the inner card and colors.surface for nested cards. A step with no override merges into the company theme rather than the platform preset. Pass null to drop the override so the step follows the company theme again. Numeric values are clamped to supported ranges. Use update_company to change the account-wide default instead.

buttonStyle.description: How primary buttons are filled: "solid" (default) or "outline" (transparent fill with a brand-color border).

buttonText.description: Label color for solid buttons. Omit to auto-derive a readable color from the button background.

content.description: Inner content card the blocks sit on. Omit to preserve its current value; when no content color is stored, the card follows background.

layout.description: Layout settings. Every field is a number except contentAlign.

contentAlign.description: Where the content column sits in a wide email client: "center" (default) or "left" (flush left, like a plain personal email; buttons, the logo and footers move left too unless set to right, or kept centered with block `styles.keepAlign: true`). Phones show the column full width either way.

presetId.description: Theme preset to base the theme on: default, soft, editorial, or bold.

typography.description: Type settings; numbers except the font-family stacks.

footerFontFamily.description: Footer font stack, also used by the auto-added footer. null removes it.

headingFontFamily.description: Font stack for headings when it differs from the email body font. Omit so headings inherit the email font.

headingFontWeight.description: Heading weight applied to all heading levels, 300-900. Omit for the per-level defaults.

headingLetterSpacing.description: Heading letter spacing in pixels (negative = tighter), clamped to -2..4. Omit for natural tracking.

fromEmail.description: From address for this step. Its domain must be configured and verified. Mutually exclusive with senderProfileId.

fromName.description: Display name override for this step. Alone it only changes the visible name; with fromEmail it also names a newly created sender profile.

html.description: Updated HTML content for imported provider markup. Raw HTML is stored as one opaque block. Sequenzy preserves that markup but does not add a company logo, branded native sections, or theme-driven block design. Use blocks for editor-native design, or a drafting prompt when you want Sequenzy to compose a new branded email. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes.

htmlContent.description: Alias for html. Raw HTML is stored as one opaque block. Sequenzy preserves that markup but does not add a company logo, branded native sections, or theme-driven block design. Use blocks for editor-native design, or a drafting prompt when you want Sequenzy to compose a new branded email. Merge tags resolve in this content but are always HTML-escaped; prefix a tag with 'html.' - e.g. {{html.subscriber.body_html}} - to insert a trusted subscriber attribute or variable holding prebuilt HTML unescaped. Injected HTML is sanitized (scripts, event handlers, and dangerous URLs stripped), must be final HTML, and renders raw only in HTML text position, never inside attributes.

nodeId.description: Optional target action_email node ID for a step. Use the nodeId returned in get_sequence.sequence.emails.

replyProfileId.description: Reply profile for this step's Reply-To. Mutually exclusive with replyTo.

replyTo.description: Reply-To address for this step. Mutually exclusive with replyProfileId.

replyToName.description: Reply-To display name override for this step. Requires replyTo; omit it when using replyProfileId, which already carries its own display name.

senderProfileId.description: Sender profile for this step's From identity. Mutually exclusive with fromEmail.

stopCondition.description: Update the sequence auto-stop condition, which is re-evaluated before every step including the first one. Example: { type: 'has_tag', value: 'customer' } ends the sequence when the subscriber has that tag. Use { type: 'entered_segment', value: 'segment_123' } to stop when they enter a segment, { type: 'field_changed', value: 'plan' } to stop when a subscriber field changes, { type: 'added_to_list', value: 'list_123' } to stop when they join a list, or { type: 'none', value: null } to clear it. The negative forms are audience guards rather than lifecycle stops: { type: 'does_not_have_tag', value: 'allowlist' } and { type: 'removed_from_list', value: 'list_123' } cancel the run before any step sends unless the subscriber carries that tag or list membership. That is how you restrict a live event or segment trigger to a chosen set of contacts without editing the graph, for example for a first pass on a production trigger or a phased rollout. Guarded-out contacts still enroll and are then cancelled at the trigger node, so they appear as cancellations there rather than in the active or waiting enrollment counts. Clearing the guard does not retry them: nothing re-enrolls them, so they only receive the sequence if the trigger fires for them again, which one-shot triggers never do, and on the one_time enrollment mode a repeated trigger is ignored too because enrollment is blocked by the existence of any earlier run rather than by its outcome. Guard a duplicate sequence and leave the real one ungated, or enroll the missed contacts afterwards with enroll_subscribers_in_sequence, which skips the one_time check.

matchConfig.description: Optional stop-condition matching, four shapes keyed by mode. event_property_filter and event_property refine event_received; field_value refines field_changed. entry_audience with audience tag/list makes a does_not_have_tag/removed_from_list guard resolve the tag or list that enrolled each contact; tag requires a tag_added trigger, and list requires a contact_added trigger scoped to at least one specific list. Omit value for this mode. Pass null to clear.

audience.description: entry_audience mode source to resolve per enrollment.

mode.description: Which matching shape the config uses. Defaults to event_property_filter when omitted and propertyFilters is present.

propertyFilters.description: event_property_filter mode: filters a stop event must all match, e.g. [{ path: 'quota_used', operator: 'greater_than', value: 1 }].

path.description: Dot-path into the stop event's properties, e.g. 'quota_used' or 'order.total'.

value.description: Comparison value (string, number, or boolean; array of values for one_of). Omit for exists/not_exists.

rules.description: event_property mode: entry-vs-stop-event field equality rules, e.g. [{ entryFieldPath: 'orderId', eventFieldPath: 'orderId' }].

type.description: Stop condition type. has_tag, added_to_list and entered_segment read the subscriber's current state before every step: the run stops at the next step whenever they have the tag, are in the list or match the segment, including when that was already true at entry. field_changed stops once the field differs from its value at entry. event_received only counts events received after enrollment - the enrolling event and earlier history never satisfy the stop. does_not_have_tag and removed_from_list stop the run whenever the subscriber lacks that tag or list membership, so they act as a required-tag or required-list allowlist for everyone the trigger enrolls.

value.description: Tag name, list ID, segment ID, field path, or event name for the stop condition. For entry_audience matching, omit this value because the enrolling tag or list is resolved per contact.

stopOnSegmentExit.description: For segment_entered, stop active enrollments when the subscriber leaves the segment.

subscriberUpdateSteps.description: Full config replacements for existing Update Subscriber steps, targeted by action_update_attributes nodeId.

config.description: Update Subscriber config. firstName, lastName, and customAttributeUpdates values may use trigger-event merge tags such as {{event.plan}}. Number and boolean values must be a literal or one standalone merge tag and are coerced after resolution.

value.description: Literal scalar, null to delete, or a standalone merge tag such as {{event.plan}}, {{event.amount}}, or {{event.active}}.

firstName.description: First name literal or merge tag; null clears the field.

lastName.description: Last name literal or merge tag; null clears the field.

tagName.description: Tag name required for a tag_added trigger replacement.

tagNames.description: Several tag names for a tag_added trigger replacement. Receiving ANY of them enrolls the contact.

timeWindowDays.description: Frequency trigger lookback window in days.

trigger.description: Atomically replace the existing dashboard trigger. Include the fields required by the new trigger type. Active sequences also require confirmLiveChange:true.

userCancellable.description: Whether subscribers may cancel their own active enrollment.

name: update_sequence

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `update_sequence` MCP tool.

appUrls.description: Dashboard URLs for relevant Sequenzy resources.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

sequence.description: The sequence record returned by Sequenzy. Run state: branch on effectiveStatus (draft, live, enrollment_paused, paused, or archived) rather than on status, which reads `active` even when new enrollments are paused. acceptsNewEnrollments and processesExistingEnrollments answer the two questions behind it, and effectiveStatusSummary is a plain-language sentence. The legacy triggerConfig.active flag is not read by the runtime; it is reported as a mirror of acceptsNewEnrollments. Email numbering: emails[].stepNumber and nodes[].config.stepNumber are legacy stored ordinals retained for compatibility. Prefer emails[].structuralStepNumber and nodes[].structuralStepNumber when explaining the visible sequence position. Structural numbers are graph-derived; emails in parallel branches intentionally share a depth. Sequences use sendingWindow for allowed local hours/days; they do not have Send Time Optimization. frequencyCapEnabled is true when email steps respect the company frequency cap (get_frequency_cap): contacts already at the cap skip the step. activeSubscribersOnly is true when only active contacts enter; when false, unsubscribed and bounced contacts still enter and only their marketing emails are skipped. STO is per-campaign (list_campaigns / get_campaign sendTimeOptimization).

completedRecipientCount.description: Recipients completed because a deleted step had no surviving successor.

migratedRecipientCount.description: Recipients moved immediately from deleted steps to their surviving successor.

subscriptionUrl.description: Owner-facing subscription, upgrade, and billing-management URL when available.

url.description: Primary dashboard URL for this result.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
